items.issue: The authored focus indicator fails WCAG 2.2 AA non-text contrast: #ff7a00 measures 2.38:1 against the paper background and 2.61:1 against white cards (1.4.11 requires 3:1), and TEST_REPORT's contrast table omits it while claiming AA verification.
items.where: styles.css:50-51 (:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--focus) … box-shadow: 0 0 0 5px var(--paper) }), styles.css:21 (--focus: #ff7a00); live tab-through at 360 showed outline rgb(255,122,0) on every control; TEST_REPORT.md:71 lists no ratio for the ring.
items.why_it_caps_score: The brief's primary goal says 'no accessibility failure' and the definition of done says 'verified contrast ratios'; a focus ring that fails the numeric AA test on every control is a checkable failure a rubric judge will find in seconds.
items.claimed_fix: :focus-visible is a two-colour ring — 3px var(--focus) outline with 3px #fff box-shadow on paper (styles.css:51), inverting to white outline + navy-deep shadow inside .top (styles.css:52); --focus var repurposed

No orange focus remains.

items.issue: The a1 hint states a false universal — 'Anything in that box is a property of the data' — but the statistics box it points at contains the 'Gap as drawn (share of the axis height)' tile, which changes with the axis (1.8% at 0-100, 45% at 70-74).

items.why_it_caps_score: It states the opposite of the data-vs-picture rule activity 1 exists to teach, so a statistics educator cannot sign off on the sentence a stuck learner reads.
items.fix: Compare the statistics box above with the chart. The first three tiles are properties of the data — they stay identical whatever the axis. The fourth tile, “gap as drawn”, is deliberately different: it is a property of the picture, because it measures the same 1.8-point gap against whatever axis you have chosen. Ask that question of anything else that moves when you drag a slider.
